Les Stokell was our next man over the long and crucial stage from Hanacross to Hickstead and our best time for this leg was Tom Carter's 30.26 in 1937, while Vern Blowfield did 30.40 in 1948. Les, however, could never seem to get really going and he was soon passed by the Blackheath runner and then A.
On Whit-Monday our team scored a good win over Portsmouth A.C. and Thames Valley H. in the team race. Les Stokell ran well to once again finish 2nd to A.
Dick Tobin was 4th, Bert Footer 6th and Bert Smith 7th. Ted Stimpson also ran a good race at Swindon in a 15 miles road race, when he finished second to A.

The ENGLISH SENIOR CROSS-COUNTRY CHAMPIONSHIP was held at Apsley over a course almost knee-deep in snow. This was definitely not a fair test to the runners, although A.A. Robertson ran in really magnificent style and fully deserved his win.
